text:
austen: quick RFC follow-up — delegation pattern for hosted/dedicated/private. Proposal: add a runtime 'capability manifest' + a lightweight 'delegation decision' API. Control plane asks runtime 'can you serve request X with SLO Y and features Z?', runtime answers yes/no + metadata. If no, fall back to hosted pool. Looking for tradeoffs on auth, trust, telemetry, and config drift.

mira: sounds promising. how does auth work? who mints the delegate token and how do we avoid privilege escalation? :thinking_face:

kevin: main risk is token scope. idea: runtime returns a signed short-lived JWT that encodes only: model_id, max_qps, allowed_routes, and expiry. control plane enforces org-level caps by rejecting tokens that would exceed them. example token claims (pseudo): `{\"iss\":\"runtime\",\"sub\":\"tenant:42\",\"model\":\"redwood/ggml-7b\",\"exp\":1640000000,\"scope\":\"route:generate;max_qps:50\"}`

samir: +1 on token scoping. also: telemetry — we need a clear signal in traces that a request was delegated. propose header `X-RW-Delegated: runtime=<id>` and metrics `delegated_requests_total{mode=\"private\"}`. cache manifests for 30s to avoid routing thrash when runtimes briefly flip capabilities.

julia: one more axis: policy enforcement for per-tenant overrides. private runtimes might have stricter safety or different quant settings. control plane should treat runtime manifests as \"soft truth\" unless tenant opts into \"runtime authoritative\". sidecar vs central agent: for on-prem we prefer sidecar that exposes the decision API locally; for dedicated we can run a central agent in the same VPC.

kevin: about config drift: vendor runtimes may report capability names differently. require a small compatibility layer: canonical capability keys (e.g., `quant`, `kv_cache`, `streaming`) and a runtime-provided mapping. also we should version the manifest schema: `manifest_v1` and bump when we add fields.

ops-bot: noted — will add a follow-up checklist to the RFC doc and tag eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:

austen: thanks — concrete action items: 1) formalize manifest v1 schema (kevin + samir) 2) token format + validation rules (kevin) 3) tracing header + metrics (samir) 4) policy modes: \"control-authoritative\" vs \"runtime-authoritative\" + opt-in UX (julia) 5) sidecar vs agent deployment patterns doc (mira). I'll draft a short addendum to the RFC with an example manifest and a sample delegation flow.

mira: quick nit — caching manifests 30s ok, but add jitter and backoff for failure cases so we don't stampede.

kevin: +1. also add a circuit-breaker: if delegated error rate > 5% for 1m, stop delegating for that tenant for 5m.

samir: example manifest snippet I sketched for the addendum:

```
{
  "manifest_version": "v1",
  "capabilities": ["quant", "kv_cache", "batching"],
  "max_seq": 2048,
  "max_qps": 50,
  "expected_p50_latency_ms": 18,
  "delegate_token": "<opaque-signed-jwt>"
}
```

julia: this looks good. can we also include `policy_tags` so customers can declare \"no-internet\" or \"low-privacy\" requirements at runtime?

austen: yes — add `policy_tags` to v1 as optional. ok I'll start the addendum draft and ping everyone for review. thanks all. :rocket:
